Challenges

Sound familiar?

“Our listings sit on page three for our main keywords.”

Amazon ranks on relevance plus sales performance. The keyword map fixes relevance first, then conversion work builds the velocity that holds rankings.

“We stuffed keywords into titles and it backfired.”

Unreadable titles kill click-through, and click-through is a ranking factor. Listings are rewritten for shoppers first, algorithms second — in that order they serve both.

“Competitors with worse products outrank us.”

Usually a backend-terms and review-velocity gap, not a product gap. The catalogue audit shows exactly where each competitor wins.

“Our A+ content looks nice but sales didn’t move.”

A+ modules are briefed against the questions and objections in your reviews — decoration doesn’t convert, answers do.

“Backend search terms are a copy-paste mess.”

Backend terms get a proper set per ASIN: no repeats, no wasted bytes, no terms already in the title.

“Variations and child ASINs are tangled.”

Variation structure affects ranking weight and reviews. The audit untangles families so equity pools instead of splitting.

“Ads make sales; organic does nothing.”

That is the most expensive way to run a store. Organic rank on core terms cuts the ad spend needed to hold position.

“We can’t tell which listings to fix first.”

Every ASIN is scored by opportunity — search volume, current rank and margin — so effort goes where the return is.

Our Process

How Amazon SEO runs

1

Catalogue audit

Listings, keywords and competitors analysed per ASIN.

2

Keyword mapping

Terms assigned to listings by relevance and opportunity.

3

Listing rebuilds

Copy, backend terms and content upgraded in priority order.

4

Track & refine

Ranks and conversion monitored; listings iterated monthly.

How It Works

A different search engine, a different playbook

Amazon's A9/A10 ranking system rewards what Google ignores: sales velocity, conversion rate and relevance signals inside the marketplace itself. Keyword stuffing a title is not a strategy.

We research how shoppers actually search on Amazon, rebuild listings around those terms, and pair them with A+ content and review strategy — so visibility and conversion climb together, which is exactly what the algorithm rewards.

  • Amazon listing audit
  • Keyword map per ASIN
  • Rewritten listings
  • A+ content briefs
  • Backend term sets
  • Rank & sales reports

FAQs

FAQs on Amazon SEO services

How is Amazon SEO different from Google SEO?

Amazon ranks by sales performance and marketplace relevance — no backlinks, no blog. The levers are keywords, conversion and velocity.

Do you manage Amazon PPC too?

Listing SEO and PPC reinforce each other; PPC management can be added through our digital marketing service.

Which marketplaces?

Amazon US, UK, and other major marketplaces — keyword research is done per marketplace.

How soon do listings improve?

Re-indexing is fast; rank movement typically shows within 2–6 weeks as conversion data updates.

Do you handle multiple marketplaces (US, UK, EU)?

Yes — keyword research and listings are done per marketplace, because shopper language and competition differ by country.

Can you work with our existing listings and brand registry assets?

Yes. The audit starts from what exists; brand registry tools like A+ and Vine are folded into the plan where you have access.
